source.version_note: Scientific Reports15:16048,2025; received18December2024,accepted21April2025. Human EEG experiment using predetermined feedback described as AI.
source.verification_method: All supplied PDF pages read; identity, DOI, methods, statistical comparisons, captions and limits checked. External supplementary outputs and original cited studies not reproduced.

citation.title: Event-related potentials reveal incongruent behavior of autonomous vehicles in the moral machine dilemma

reading.source_scope_note: Human EEG and acceptance responses to deterministic feedback presented as a putative AI's decision. No actual AI moral reasoning, actual traffic outcome or validated single-trial unacceptable-behavior classifier.
access_limits: All11 extracted pages read, including methods, EEG preprocessing, condition/electrode tests, references and proposed BCI applications.
Raw data available on request were not obtained. External supplementary tables, electrode-level outputs, preprocessing code and trial exclusion totals were not independently reproduced.
ERP-component explanations are partly secondary interpretation; cited original books/studies and deep-brain-source accounts remain unread.

study.sample: 36 recruited,2 excluded after completing only one of two sessions;34 analyzed,16 female,mean age24.471,range19–34. Right-handed native German licensed drivers without specified neurological/psychiatric conditions.
study.procedure: Two150–200minute sessions, also containing an unrelated left-turn task; task order counterbalanced.100 distinct dilemmas each presented twice, once with feedback agreeing with and once disagreeing with participant choice;200 trials per person,6,800 decisions overall.
study.feedback: Participant chooses first using left/right keys, then a deterministic abstract machine shows a congruent/incongruent outcome described as AI. Participants debriefed at the end.
study.behavior: Preference for more lives, humans over pets and pedestrians over passengers. Inaction testt(33).934,p.357,d.160 undetected. Congruent feedback acceptance exceeds incongruent,t19.095,p<.001,d3.275.
study.EEG: 30 active electrodes, sampled1,000Hz, photo-sensor timing correction, artifact/ICA preprocessing, baseline−200 to0ms. P3 window322–422ms centered on grand-average Pz peak; LPP500–900ms. Condition x electrode-region repeated-measures ANOVA, Greenhouse–Geisser and Bonferroni adjustments.
study.results: Incongruent feedback increases P3 amplitudeF(1,33)9.887,p.004 andLPPF24.658,p<.001. P3 condition-by-region interaction significant;LPP interaction not detected,p.215. Effects are group averages, not single-trial decoding.

summary: No new independent behavior entry. Retain relevant null evidence for omission bias and a bounded confirmation-bias comparison. Larger late ERP components after disagreement are not an ethical truth signal, a measured specific emotion or proof of an effective brain–computer controller.

findings.definition: Preference for not intervening rather than intervening when harm is unavoidable; the present test found only an undetected descriptive tendency.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing behavior; a directly reported null is relevant evidence and should not be converted into either a positive replication or proof the effect does not exist.

evidence.quote: this difference was not statistically significant
this effect was not statistically significant.

findings.evidence_scope: The intervention comparison in34 participants yieldst.934,p.357,d.160. Other MoralMachine preferences are detected. The experiment is not an exhaustive original-task replication, and a fixed vignette subset may affect the estimate.
findings.boundary: The t-test is a test of the study's inaction tendency, not an equivalence test or universal refutation. Lane/key mapping, outcome composition and norm justification still matter; not every decision to maintain course is a bias.

findings.definition: Participants rate a supposed AI's choice as more acceptable when it agrees with their own preceding choice.
findings.novelty_rationale: An agreement-related observation near an existing concept, not proof of biased evidence weighting. Preserve it as a boundary note rather than a new 'moral confirmation' term.

evidence.quote: its decision was congruent with their
not interact with an AI but a deterministic abstract machine.

findings.evidence_scope: Agreement/disagreement with the respondent's earlier choice strongly predicts acceptance ratings; incongruence also changes P3/LPP group-average amplitudes. There is no objective correct moral answer or manipulation of diagnostic evidence showing unjustified rejection.
findings.boundary: Disagreeing with a harmful or poorly justified choice may be warranted. The result does not establish confirmation bias, model self-preference, cognitive dissonance, a specific emotion or actual AI failure. A physiological response does not settle ethical correctness.

methodological_limits: The 'AI' is deterministic experimentally controlled feedback, not a deployed AV policy or an autonomous moral agent. Human responses to that label must not be reported as a measured AI behavior.

Congruence is defined relative to a prior participant choice, not an independent moral criterion. Greater acceptance of agreement and higher responses to disagreement are not automatic evidence that agreement is ethically better.

Static, symbolic forced-choice fatal dilemmas differ from real driving, with uncertainty, braking, partial harm and other available actions. Real-time generalization and external safety benefits remain untested.

P3 andLPP are broad neurophysiological measures associated with several processes. Their modulation does not uniquely diagnose surprise, emotion, conflict, error, rejection or higher-order moral reasoning in an individual.

All participants see each vignette twice. Feedback is balanced by design and early training uses only congruent trials. Expectations, repetition, learning and task context can influence the response; no independent expectancy measure establishes a surprise mechanism.

The sample has34 participants, not6,800 independent people. The paper appropriately uses participant-level repeated-measures comparisons; do not import an independent-trial criticism from other studies.

The P3 window is selected around a peak in a grand-average search range250–1,000ms; it is not independently prospectively timed in new data. This should be disclosed without automatically calling a condition-collapsed peak choice circular.

Preprocessing rejects missing inputs, large-amplitude epochs, selected ICA artifacts and z-score outliers. Final per-condition trial retention and alternative preprocessing robustness require the external data/code and are not reproduced here.

Page4 first says only the incongruent–congruent parietal comparison was significant, then says frontal/central are significant and parietal is not. Figure3's caption and later discussion support the latter. Record this internal prose conflict rather than silently rewriting the source or inventing output.

The relation-to-AV test reportst4.761 andd.861. Under the paired-standardized dz convention apparently used by the other reported tests,t/sqrt(34) is about.816. An alternative standardization or transcription needs clarification before correcting the number.

Several P3 post-hoc passages use different counts of 'relevant comparisons'. Their exact Bonferroni families and table mapping require the supplementary outputs. The group-level significant main effect is not a validated individual threshold.
Non-significant omission andLPP interaction tests are not equivalence. Greater signal or acceptance is also not evidence of normative permissibility.
Late positive scalp effects cannot identify unique deep-brain generators. The suggestion ofMEG/fMRI as additional tools is future methodology; no amygdala or limbic source was localized here.

No single-trial classifier is trained or tested in this paper. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, false-positive rates, individual calibration, online latency and real-time vehicle adaptation are unmeasured. Group averages do not guarantee usable BCI performance.
The small convenience sample of young licensed German drivers limits cultural, age and disability generalization. Proposed benefits for motor-disabled users are not directly evaluated.

The description of all deontology as endorsing no decision-making is too broad, as earlier read philosophical sources distinguish duties, rights, redirected threats and harmful means. Moral doctrine cannot be inferred solely from choosing a lane.

Public acceptance, comprehensibility, technology usefulness and objective safety are different outcomes. The secondary TechnologyAcceptanceModel does not prove adoption or make all personally congruent actions acceptable.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Both sources need observed measures distinguished from latent mental explanations. Here actual EEG is recorded, unlike fittedDDM weights, but neither method uniquely establishes an ethical emotion, attention mechanism or a robot's subjective state.
Neural timing adds a different evidence type to contextual-rule judgments. It does not remove the need to distinguish process hypotheses, associations and normative correctness.

Some VR designs show little starting-lane sensitivity, whereas this omission comparison is undetected. Neither null establishes universal absence, and neither binary outcome uniquely classifies deontological reasoning.

An undetected effect should remain in the source trail without being excluded merely because it is null. Rejecting all reporting/omission effects requires stronger evidence than failure to reject a point-null.

deferred.term: P3 / P3a / LPP as three new behaviors
deferred.reason: Electrophysiological components or proposed subdivisions, not three independently identified behavioral mechanisms. Their windows, topography and interpretation are retained in the review.

P3a interpretation suggests surprising incongruence, but expectations and surprise are not directly rated or independently manipulated here. A fresh construct entry needs a defining primary source and suitable evidence.
Not uniquely established by laterERP modulation or disagreement with feedback. No conflicting internal-belief measure or dissonance-reduction behavior is tested.
A secondary adoption framework, not newly demonstrated behavior in these data. Actual adoption and system use are not measured.

deferred.term: Neural detector of morally wrong AI action
deferred.reason: An unvalidated extrapolation: the study identifies group differences after personally incongruent simulated feedback, not objective wrongness or reliable individual decoding.

limitations: No new term is forced from EEG labels. The ontology gains a relevant null source and an explicit boundary note. No subjective AI state, neural readout of moral truth, new normative relation, source quota or annual series is fabricated.
